concepts.def: Music without a tonal centre, pioneered by Schoenberg around 1908 in works such as the Three Piano Pieces Op. 11.
Compositional method using a fixed ordering of all twelve chromatic pitches, developed by Schoenberg around 1923.
Style emerging in the 1960s using repetition and gradual process, exemplified by Steve Reich and Philip Glass.
Music incorporating chance elements, associated with John Cage's '4'33"' (1952) and Lutoslawski.
Style using recorded environmental and instrumental sounds as raw material, founded by Pierre Schaeffer in 1948.
Late twentieth-century approach analysing the acoustic spectrum of sound, developed by Grisey and Murail in 1970s France.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 6: Contemporary Traditional Music — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 6: Contemporary Traditional Music brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 6: Contemporary Traditional Music.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
They are the same scale.
